subject: VPC fee & ops structure — Acme Health proposal and options
messages:
From: Jenna Cole <jenna.cole@acmehealth.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: Acme Health Procurement <procurement@acmehealth.com>
Date: 2026-11-10T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Private deployment pricing: initial asks

Hi Michael —

Thanks for taking this. We’re evaluating Redwood for a VPC/on-prem deployment across several datacenters. Before we loop in finance, can you provide a ballpark commercial structure for: 1) on-prem license (per-GPU vs per-node vs metered), 2) platform fee (annual vs monthly; capitalization guidance), 3) support tiers and response targets (business hours vs 24/7 + phone), and 4) migration/implementation credits or professional services offsets for a multi-datacenter rollout?

We expect an initial install in 3 regions with ~8 x A100-equivalent GPUs per region to start (scale later). Target timeline: proof-of-concept in Q1, production in Q2 2027.

Also: any standard runbook or ops checklist you can share (install, KMS integration, backup/restore expectations) would help us scope internal work.

If you can send a SKU-style matrix and a short note on typical commercial levers (commit discounts, early-payment terms, migration credits), that’ll be perfect. Happy to set a 30-minute call after you send details.

Thanks,
Jenna Cole
Head of IT Procurement
Acme Health

Subject: RE: Private deployment pricing: initial asks

Hi Jenna —

Appreciate the clear ask. Summary below and I attached a detailed matrix (vpc-pricing-matrix.xlsx) and support SLA overview (support_sla_matrix.pdf):

1) License model options
   - Per-GPU perpetual license + annual platform fee (common for on-prem customers who capitalize software). Example: $X per A100-equivalent GPU perpetual + 12% annual platform fee.
   - Metered consumption (tokens/throughput) for mixed-hosted/onprem setups — better for bursty workloads, typically higher unit price but lower upfront.
   - Node-based flat (per inference node) for customers wanting predictable unit pricing across heterogenous hardware.

2) Platform fee structure
   - Annual invoiced platform fee (recommended) or monthly edition. Annual invoices can be capitalized; we provide a letter of support for capitalization for accounting. We list a standard platform fee as a percentage of license value; see matrix.

3) Support tiers
   - Standard (business hours email, 24-48h initial response), Enhanced (24/7 email + 4h P1), Premium (24/7 phone + 1h P1, includes one onsite enablement week).

4) Migration/implementation credits
   - We offer a migration credit program: up to $50k offset on PS fees for commitments >= 12 months or spend threshold. We can convert this to a discount on the first-year platform fee.

Commercial levers we typically use: 12–36 month committed capacity discounts (10–30% depending on term and commit), prepayment discounts (up to 5%), and an additional bundling credit for including managed enablement.

Next steps: I’ve attached the matrix; if the A100-equivalent GPU counts are correct I’ll produce a line-item quote with a few alternative packaging scenarios (perpetual + annual fee vs metered). Can we do a 30-minute call Thursday 11/12 at 10am PT to review?

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Enterprise Sales Engineering
Redwood Inference
michael_grant@redwood.com

Attachments: vpc-pricing-matrix.xlsx, support_sla_matrix.pdf

Quick legal/commercial notes from our side:

- Seat vs metered: if Acme opts for perpetual per-GPU licenses, we will include a license schedule tied to serial numbers and an audit right clause with 60-day cure. For metered models we use usage reports with monthly reconciliation.
- Platform fee capitalization: we can provide a standard capitalization support letter and include language in the license schedule to facilitate finance.
- Acceptance window: standard is 30 days after deployment; we can extend to 45 days for this deal in exchange for a modest concession (an additional 5% on the platform fee for year one) — optional but useful for regulated environments that need extended validation.
- Export/third-party SW: small note to ensure Acme’s on-prem stack components (e.g., HSM vendor) are cleared; we can add a compatibility appendix to the SOW.

If you want, I’ll prepare a short redline to the standard license schedule that includes the 45-day acceptance and capitalization language.

—Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Hi Jenna — a couple of ops details that should help your engineering team scope:

- Runbook & KMS: attached is a trimmed sample runbook (onprem-runbook-sample.txt). We support KMS integrations (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, and common HSM vendors). We typically recommend customer-managed keys for on-prem for compliance; Redwood supports KeyWrap and encrypted KV cache at rest.
- Install/upgrade cadence: we publish a minor update cadence (quarterly) and a security patch cadence (as-needed). Patch windows are coordinated with your on-call.
- Observability: the private control plane can forward tokenized telemetry to your Splunk/Elastic endpoint; full traces are available under a customer-managed retention policy.
- On-site enablement: included with Premium support (one week). For the architecture you described, expect ~5 engineer-days of professional services per region to bring to production (we can absorb part of that under the migration credit program).

I’m happy to join the call on Thursday to walk the runbook and KMS options.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.com
